subtype: Approach: making questions and answering from memory [Thinking]
passage: Note from the Class 6 tutor, Thursday evening. Sahil sat with his science book and a pencil. Sahil made a question out of every heading. The one on seasons became, "Why is winter colder than summer?" Then he closed the book and answered aloud. "Because the earth is far from the sun?" He stopped, frowned and opened the book. "No. The tilt changes how the light falls." He ticked the right ones and put a cross by the wrong ones. Then he went back to read only the crossed topics. I did not tell him the answers. I only asked what he would study again. Himani, tutor

qa.q: What question did Sahil make from a heading?
qa.a: He asked, "Why is winter colder than summer?"

qa.q: What did Sahil feel when he stopped, frowned and checked the book after his first answer?
qa.a: He felt unsure and a bit puzzled, since he suspected his answer was wrong. Checking gave him the right idea.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Sahil use to check his answers, and why?
qa.a: He could ask a friend to ask the questions from the book. Hearing someone else's questions covers parts he may not think to ask.

qa.q: How does the tutor Himani see Sahil's method?
qa.a: Himani sees a boy who finds his own gaps and works on them, which is why Himani only asked what he would study again.

grounding: A boy turns each heading into a question and answers aloud with the book closed, and checking wrong answers tells him exactly what to study again.
